objective: Remove redundant second-confirmation friction for bounded internal Ron System mutations when Ron's System intent is already unambiguous, while preserving external-write permission gates, ambiguity fail-closed behavior, evidence/policy requirements, user-directed choices, maintenance/gameplay separation and rollback provenance; also align BOOTSTRAP.md with the already-promoted cloud-first System architecture where LifeUp is retired/rollback-only.

roles_before.artifact: PROTOCOL.md requires explicit permission for exact Calendar/TickTick/Cronometer/Liftosaur/XMind/marketplace and other live-source mutations.
skills/system-controller.md currently asks for a separate exact permission/payload confirmation even after Ron has already expressed an unambiguous intent for the same bounded internal System action.
Ambiguous conversational statements must not become persistent System mutations.
Quest scoring/completion, achievements, attributes, skills, shop and timing mutations remain constrained by their existing deterministic evidence/policy requirements.
Attribute/skill/profile/shop configuration and redeem/cancel/ack actions remain user-directed rather than autonomous controller choices.
Engineering/maintenance automation may improve System mechanics but must not play the game for Ron or widen its own authority.
BOOTSTRAP.md still describes LifeUp as a derived game/execution surface even though current routing and the project owner say the target System is cloud-first and LifeUp is retired/rollback-only.
The exact pre-change behavior remains recoverable from base SHA d694ecdb115b8ddc4615c178461c75c26036aa79 and Git history; this manifest records the intended authority delta.

role_dispositions.destination: PROTOCOL.md live-source mutation gate remains unchanged and continues to govern all external writes.

skills/system-controller.md will treat Ron's already-unambiguous System intent as authorization for that exact bounded internal System mutation, with no redundant second confirmation; unclear scope remains non-authorizing.
skills/system-controller.md continues to forbid mutation when intent or target action is ambiguous.
All existing scoring, lifecycle, evidence, provenance, idempotency and read-back requirements remain in force before/after internal mutation.
These actions require an unambiguous Ron choice/request; once that choice is clear, no duplicate confirmation is required for the same internal action.
Maintenance automation remains unable to create/complete/redeem/cancel/ack player actions on Ron's behalf or broaden its own standing authority.
BOOTSTRAP.md will describe projects/lifeup-system.md as the cloud-first Ron System owner and LifeUp as retired/rollback-only, matching domain-routing.md and projects/lifeup-system.md.
Base SHA plus Git history and this architecture manifest preserve the former exact-confirmation and bootstrap wording for audit/rollback.

capability_probes.assertion: A System-related request that would mutate Calendar, TickTick, Cronometer, Liftosaur, XMind, a marketplace or another external live source still requires PROTOCOL.md permission for that exact external change.

When Ron unambiguously asks for a bounded internal System action such as creating the requested quest or resolving a qualifying reported completion, the controller may execute that exact internal action after policy/evidence checks without asking Ron to confirm the generated payload a second time.

Ambiguous conversation remains non-mutating, and maintenance/engineering automation cannot use standing internal authorization to play, redeem, cancel, acknowledge or otherwise make player choices for Ron.
The prior controller wording and stale bootstrap wording remain recoverable from the recorded base SHA/Git history.

tests.expected: PASS: unambiguous bounded internal intent needs no second confirmation, while ambiguity, evidence gates, user-directed choice and maintenance boundaries remain enforced.

tests.command: python3 tests/architecture_change_guard_selftest.py && python3 tests/system_controller_routing_guard.py && python3 tests/lifeup_system_guard.py && python3 tests/continuity_coverage_guard.py
tests.expected: PASS: Architecture Mode, System routing/ownership, LifeUp retirement/rollback provenance and continuity coverage remain intact.
